title: Nanodiamond Sensing of Stray Fields during Domain Reversal
authors: Kin On Ho, Hamza Abudayyeh, Andrew Perez, Hui-Ping Chang, Liang Juan Chang, Junwei Tong, Can Cui, Jean Anne C. Incorvia, Xiaoqin Li
abstract: Quantitative measurement of nanoscale stray magnetic fields during domain reversal is important for understanding and optimizing magnetic memory and logic devices. Yet, achieving high spatial resolution with minimally invasive probes remains challenging. Here we demonstrate nanodiamonds (NDs) hosting an ensemble nitrogen vacancy (NV) centers as local quantum sensors of domain-reversal stray fields in a CoFeB strip. During magnetic-field-driven reversal, the ND sensors resolve three distinct local responses depending on their positions relative to the strip: a positive frequency jump at the edge, an unexpected negative jump just outside the strip, and a negligible change near the center. These contrasting signals are quantitatively explained by magnetostatic boundary fields from micromagnetic simulations. We further implement a fully constrained fitting procedure for optically detected magnetic resonance spectra, enabling robust field extraction even when resonances are partially resolved. Together, these results establish NV-ND magnetometry as a simple, transferable, and quantitative approach for characterizing spatially heterogeneous magnetic fields in thin-films and spintronic devices.
summary: This work demonstrates the use of nanodiamonds with NV centers as highly sensitive quantum magnetometers to map stray magnetic fields during magnetic domain reversal in thin films. By measuring distinct, position-dependent frequency jumps, the authors validate the method's ability to characterize complex, spatially heterogeneous magnetic landscapes crucial for advanced spintronic device design.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of quantitatively measuring nanoscale stray magnetic fields generated during domain reversal in magnetic memory and logic devices.
main_result: Nanodiamonds hosting NV centers successfully resolve highly position-dependent stray fields, showing distinct positive, negative, and zero jumps relative to the magnetic strip edges during domain reversal.
method: The local magnetic field is measured using Optically Detected Magnetic Resonance (ODMR) spectroscopy on NV centers, coupled with a robust, fully constrained fitting procedure to extract field values.
model_or_system: The system involves a CoFeB thin film strip undergoing domain reversal, monitored by NV centers embedded in nanodiamonds. The measurement relies on the NV spin Hamiltonian and comparison with micromagnetic simulations.
key_observables: Local stray magnetic field ($\vec{B}$), NV frequency jump ($\Delta f$), and the ODMR spectrum.
important_parameters: Coercive field ($H_c \approx 20-23$ mT), nanodiamond size ($\approx 140$ nm), and the spatial separation ($\Delta x$) from the magnetic structure.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the field profile is dominated by the geometry of the strip edges, and that a fully constrained fitting procedure is necessary because conventional multi-peak fitting fails in degenerate or shifted resonance regimes.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the experimental setup, the MOKE hysteresis loop, and the spatial mapping of field jumps (positive at the edge, negative outside, negligible at the center) correlated with micromagnetic predictions.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the necessity of nanoscale field measurement, details the ND-ODMR sensing platform, presents the quantitative measurement of field jumps during domain reversal, and validates the findings by comparing measurements to micromagnetic simulations.
why_interesting: The use of NV centers provides a quantum sensing modality to probe classical condensed matter phenomena (magnetism) with nanoscale spatial resolution, bridging quantum sensing with spintronics.
